tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/NumberFieldArithm.targets: The classical arithmetic of a number-field extension packaged for LMFDB-style invariants: the splitting/decomposition dictionary, Frobenius elements and the Artin symbol and ideal-theoretic Artin map, the power-basis index with Dedekind-Kummer and Dedekind's theorem on cycle types, the relative discriminant ideal, the global-local dictionary at finite places, higher-ramification consequences (different and discriminant exponents), monogenicity and explicit units, and an intrinsic label predicate with a worked suite of fields.
baselineHas: NumberField.artinSymbol (TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/ArtinSymbol.lean:57) with its comparison API, and the relative Frobenius IsArithFrobAt with existence, uniqueness at unramified primes and restriction along AlgEquiv.restrictNormal
TauCeti.relDiscr (TauCeti/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/Discriminant/Basic.lean:35), at Dedekind generality, with non-vanishing, the tower formula, ramifiedSupport and Stickelberger's congruence
Mathlib's Ideal.sum_ramification_inertia, KummerDedekind, differentIdeal with transitivity, Ideal.relNorm, IsDecompositionField/IsInertiaField, and Dirichlet's unit theorem with the regulator
TauCeti's IsNonarchimedeanLocalField instance on v.adicCompletion K with the residue field and its cardinality (Layer 5.1, fully built)
missing: Layer 5, the completion dictionary: the semilocal equivalence K_v (x) L = prod_{w|v} L_w, norm/trace product formulas, e/f matching, decompositionHom identifying the decomposition group with the local Galois group, the integral-closure package on completed integer rings, and localization of the different

Layer 6: the local lower ramification filtration does not exist for these completions (the only filtration in the baseline is TauCeti's for places of a function field), so the different-exponent formula v_Q(d) = sum_i (#G_i - 1), the tame/wild exponents and the permutation-action discriminant formula cannot be stated

Scattered top-of-layer items: 1.5 (splitting in the Galois closure and composita), 3.7/3.9-3.11 (Dedekind's criterion, Dedekind's theorem on cycle types, common index divisors), 4.2's relDiscr_localization, 7.1's subfield dictionary and 7.4's explicit unit certification
Layer 8: the intrinsic label predicate, the page-coverage map and the worked five-field suite
Imports nothing from other roadmaps: the whole stack is classical algebraic number theory over Mathlib's Dedekind-domain and local-field substrate, which is already present

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/QuadraticFormInva.targets: The invariant theory of quadratic forms over a field: square classes and chain equivalence, Witt theory, quaternion algebras and the four-fold splitting criterion, dimension/discriminant/Hasse/Clifford invariants, the Witt ring and its fundamental ideal with Pfister forms, the classification of forms over a nonarchimedean local field (dyadic case included), the identification Br(K) = H^2(G_K, (K^sep)^x) at the mu_2 level, Stiefel-Whitney classes, and the Scharlau transfer with Kahn's relative Stiefel-Whitney formula.
baselineHas: Mathlib's QuadraticForm/QuadraticMap with diagonalization, isometries, Equivalent, tensor products and a full CliffordAlgebra directory; QuaternionAlgebra with its Basis universal property

TauCeti's square-class group with its multiplicative avatar and finiteness, Represents/unitValueSet with the representation criterion, binary normal forms, Witt's chain-equivalence theorem and RegularFormClass as the quotient (Layer 0)

TauCeti's hyperbolic plane, Witt decomposition and cancellation, reflections with Cartan-Dieudonne and Witt's extension theorem (Layer 1); discr and signedDiscr with the sum/product/scaling formulas (Layer 3)

TauCeti.BrauerGroup with its CommGroup structure and base change (TauCeti/Algebra/BrauerGroup/BaseChange.lean), the CentralSimple directory, the local-field normalized valuation with unit filtration and graded pieces, and a low-degree continuous cup product with corestriction
missing: Layer 4: the Witt-Grothendieck and Witt rings, the fundamental ideal I(K) with I/I^2 = K^x/(K^x)^2, and Pfister forms with roundness and the isotropic-iff-hyperbolic criterion

Layer 5: the quaternion symbol [(a,b)] in Br(K) with bilinearity and the Steinberg value, the Hasse invariant s(q) = prod_{i<j} [(a_i,a_j)], the Clifford invariant and the I^2 homomorphism (grep for hasseInvariant/pfister/wittRing finds nothing in either library)

Layer 6: the quadratic defect as a fractional ideal, the {+-1}-valued Hilbert symbol with bimultiplicativity and nondegeneracy, the local classification by (dim, d, s) including the dyadic case, u(K) = 4, and the agreement of the two Hasse invariants with the local invariant map

Layer 7: Br(K) = H^2(G_K, (K^sep)^x) via crossed products, the comparison iota : H^2(G_K, mu_2) -> Br(K)[2], and the cup-norm theorem - Hilbert 90 for G_K and the Kummer isomorphism are themselves missing
Layers 8-9: w_1 and w_2 as cup products of Kummer classes with iota(hasse) = w_2, the Scharlau transfer along a K-linear functional and Kahn's relative Stiefel-Whitney formula
Imports nothing from other roadmaps; the substrates it consumes (Brauer group, central simple algebras, local fields, low-degree Galois cohomology) are already in Tau Ceti

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge.targets: Construct the Jacobian of a smooth projective geometrically integral curve X/k as an abelian variety of dimension g, representing Pic^0_{X/k}, together with the Abel-Jacobi morphism aj : X -> Jac X and its Albanese universal property, with base-change compatibility.
baselineHas: TauCeti's scheme Weil and Cartier divisors with equivCartierDivisor (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/WeilDivisor/Scheme/Cartier/Inverse.lean) and O_X(D) locally free of rank one

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Cohomology/Basic.lean) with long exact and Mayer-Vietoris sequences and a truncated Euler characteristic, plus InvertibleSheaf.tensorProduct
TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AbelianVariety/ with the category, Hom groups, products, base change, dim, Isogeny, TangentSpace and commutativity from Mathlib's rigidity theorem

Riemann-Roch, genus, Weil-differential duality and deg K = 2g-2 for algebraic function fields (TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Differential/CanonicalDivisor.lean) - but not for schemes, and with no bridge to curves
missing: Layer B, coherent cohomology of schemes over k: acyclicity of affines, Cech = derived on a separated scheme, finite-dimensionality for proper X/k, vanishing above dimension, scheme-level genus, Riemann-Roch and Serre duality with the relative dualizing sheaf omega_{X/k}; also deg L := chi(L) - chi(O_X) and its agreement with the divisor degree, and Pic X as a group (line bundles have no duals yet)

Layer C, the whole relative theory: higher direct images along proper flat finitely presented morphisms with coherence, flat base change, cohomology-and-base-change/semicontinuity (Grauert), the theorem on formal functions, relative effective Cartier divisors, and Sym^d X as a scheme

Layer D, the crux: Pic_{X/k} as the fppf sheafification of T -> Pic(X_T)/Pic(T), rigidification along x_0 with the Poincare bundle, Pic^0 as an open-and-closed component, representability by either the Abel-map/Sym^d route or the general Grothendieck Picard scheme, and properness/projectivity of Pic^0
Layer E's remainder: T_0 Pic^0 = H^1(X,O_X) and dim Jac = g, the theorems of the cube and square, the dual abelian variety, and polarizations via the theta divisor
Layer F: the Abel-Jacobi morphism, the Albanese universal property, and base change along k -> K
Imports nothing from other roadmaps, but neither library has any higher direct image, Serre duality for schemes, or Picard functor (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry has no such directory)

Mathlib's groupCohomology and group homology via the bar complex (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupCohomology/Basic.lean:186), plus abstract spectral sequences of spectral objects

missing: H.2: homotopy fibres and homotopy pullbacks, the fibration long exact sequence with the degree-0/1 pointed-set distinction, comparison of Kan-simplicial with topological homotopy groups, Quillen's Theorems A and B, and the bisimplicial diagonal comparison - none of it in either library

H.3: the plus construction by attaching 2- and 3-cells, pi_1(X^+_P) = pi_1(X)/P with the homology isomorphism, the acyclic-map universal property; the Hurewicz theorem its tests need is also absent (grep for hurewicz finds nothing)
H.4: group completion via Segal Gamma-spaces, the group-completion theorem with its homology-localisation hypothesis, and cofinal stabilisation to BGL(R)^+

H.5: any model of spectra at all - suspension spectra, loops and shift, integer-indexed stable homotopy groups, fibre/cofibre sequences, the stable homotopy category with fibrant/cofibrant replacement, and smash products; Mathlib has no spectra
H.6: E/m and the Bockstein sequence, p-completion as a derived inverse limit, the Milnor lim^1 sequence, exact couples with convergence, and arithmetic fracture squares

missing: SV.0-SV.1: sieve dimension kappa as a hypothesis on local densities, lower-bound sieves, the optimised Selberg bound X/G(sqrt D), Brun's combinatorial sieve, the fundamental lemma in its proved ranges, and Brun-Titchmarsh and Brun's twin-prime theorem
SV.2: the additive and multiplicative large sieve inequalities, the duality principle for bilinear forms, and Vaughan's identity with Type I/II decompositions
SV.3: Siegel-Walfisz and Bombieri-Vinogradov
SV.4: admissible tuples and the whole Maynard-Tao multidimensional sieve giving bounded gaps and clusters
SV.5: the beta sieve, Chen's theorem and the affine sieve

Imports only AnalyticNumberTheory AN.0-AN.3 (zero-free regions, PNT-type estimates) and elementary finite-field character sums FF.0/FF.1; its closure is 9 external stages over 3 roadmaps - the objects it reasons about all exist already, only the estimates are missing

Mathlib's torus and finite-group character orthogonality, Dirichlet's approximation theorem, one-variable Hensel, Chevalley-Warning and Euler products
Mathlib's Lagrange four-squares theorem and Dirichlet's theorem on primes in progressions

QuadraticFormInvariants has its bottom four layers largely built in Tau Ceti (square classes and chain equivalence, Witt decomposition and cancellation, quaternion norm forms, discriminants) and its missing Witt ring, Hasse/Clifford invariants, Hilbert symbol, local classification and Br(K) = H^2(G_K, mu_2) all sit one or two steps above existing BrauerGroup, CentralSimple, Clifford-algebra and local-field theory.

ExponentialSums contains three of SieveMethods' six stages in its upstream closure (it needs SV.2's large sieve and Vaughan identities for the three-primes theorem) and then adds, above them, the l-adic Weil/Deligne bounds through FF.2 and Vinogradov's mean value theorem with decoupling - 78 external stages over 15 roadmaps against SieveMethods' 9 over 3. SieveMethods' own missing theory (Brun's sieve and the fundamental lemma, the large sieve, Bombieri-Vinogradov, Maynard-Tao) is a strict sub-part of what ExponentialSums must also have.

JacobianChallenge must build a deep vertical tower of scheme theory that has no analogue in the baseline: coherent cohomology with affine acyclicity, finiteness for proper X/k and Serre duality with omega_{X/k}; then higher direct images with flat base change, cohomology-and-base-change, formal functions and Sym^d X; then the fppf sheafification Pic_{X/k} with rigidification and representability, and the dual abelian variety and polarizations. SieveMethods needs many hard estimates (the fundamental lemma of sieve theory, the large sieve, Bombieri-Vinogradov, Maynard-Tao) but almost no new objects - Mathlib already supplies BoundingSieve/SelbergSieve with Lambda^2 weights, Dirichlet characters and L-functions, so its stack rests on theory that exists.

ArithmeticQuantumTopology needs both a whole new topological development (framed-link categories, surgery presentations and the Kirby move theorem, ribbon categories with quantum traces, U_q(sl_2) at roots of unity and the Reshetikhin-Turaev normalization, then colored Jones and Habiro expansions, then ideal triangulations with extended Bloch classes and regulators) and, through K3BlochGroups V.3/V.5, the entire algebraic K-theory tower - 153 external stages over 35 roadmaps at depth 13.
